GPS & maps

Remember where the day took you.

Some trips stay in one place. Others unfold across miles of river, shoreline, open water, or back roads. Keep the geography with the memory.

Trip route · Catch locations

Optional GPS route tracking

Turn on route tracking when you want a record of where you traveled during a trip.

Use it while walking a river, wading, fishing from shore, kayaking, canoeing, trolling, fishing from a boat, or moving between nearby spots.

The route belongs
to the story.

See catches in context

A catch is easier to remember when you can see where it happened. Catch locations can become part of the route and trip record.

Keep places connected to trips

A saved location is more useful when you know which days happened there. Cast Your Line keeps places tied to the fishing history around them.

Look back at the route, not just the destination

Years later, a line on a map can bring back details that a place name alone cannot—the bend in the river, the shoreline you walked, the stretch where you kept stopping, the path you took across the lake.

That movement is part of the day too.
